title: Length of a flattened range
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let $f$ assign a finite list to each natural number. If $\text{length}(f(z))=k$ for every natural number $z<n$, then concatenating the lists $f(0),\ldots,f(n-1)$ gives a list of length $nk$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps each natural number to a list
